A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KAN research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–F support comparison; relocated material and renumbered tables can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original function-fitting, PDE, continual-learning, knot-theory and Anderson-localization experiments, plus LAN image-fitting results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the appendix experiments. The separately attributed Shi Lab result is not needed to establish this assessment.

M1.justification: Section 2.2 changes the specified residual activation from w(b(x)+spline(x)) to w_b b(x)+w_s spline(x), with separately trainable scales and revised initialization. This is a limited parameterization revision; the KAN architecture, grid extension, sparsification, pruning, symbolic conversion and appendix LAN method remain otherwise unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same toy tasks, special functions, Feynman equations, Poisson problem, continual-learning scenario, knot data, Anderson models and appendix image-fitting task. Removing PDE superiority from the abstract does not remove the PDE experiment.

E2.justification: The knot-classification comparison gains a reported compact-MLP comparator: v4 Table 3's caption attributes 80% accuracy with 60 parameters to Shi Lab. This is an external result, not a documented new evaluation by the authors. The existing table rows and other comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 3.3 changes the reported Feynman MLP width from 20 to 5, retaining the depth sweep and activation choices. Section 2.2 also specifies w_s=1 and Xavier initialization for w_b instead of a shared Xavier-initialized scale. These are reported setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: The knot-feature ablations, continual-learning demonstration, LAN interpretability analyses, Appendix C hyperparameter study and Appendix E grid-size failure observation are retained. New qualifications about these experiments do not add robustness tests or ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions report three random seeds for the special-function and Feynman sweeps, and seeds 0–99 under two regularization strengths for unsupervised knot learning. No confidence intervals, significance tests or new uncertainty-reporting practices are added.

E6.justification: v4 adds the externally attributed 60-parameter MLP result at 80% accuracy. Existing empirical table values and plotted results are retained, including the 81.6% KAN and 78.0% DeepMind MLP knot results. The Feynman width revision therefore does not establish a same-setting performance change; the PDE 100-fold comparison is relocated from the introduction.

T1.justification: Limited formal revisions include the separately scaled residual-activation definition in Eq. (2.10) and correction of the incoming-edge score in Eq. (2.21). Theorem 2.1, its smoothness assumptions, approximation bound and proof are unchanged. The removed scaling-exponent table's mathematical content remains in the prose.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and final recommendation qualify KAN advantages as applying to small-scale AI + Science tasks. The abstract restricts its accuracy comparison to function fitting, while the introduction presents PDE solving as a simple Poisson demonstration. The central architecture, scaling and interpretability contributions remain.

C2.justification: v4 adds specific qualifications about symbolic PDE solutions favoring KANs, untested advanced optimization methods, and unclear locality in high-dimensional continual learning. It also distinguishes compositional approximation from finite-sample generalization and discusses limitations on escaping dimensionality in general function spaces.

D1.justification: The implementation description now specifies separate base/spline scales, their default trainability and initialization. The Feynman baseline-width specification is revised, and the toy comparison explicitly excludes optimizer switching and boosting. The pykan access instructions and Appendix A functionality documentation remain substantively unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 substantially expands theoretical positioning through prior Kolmogorov-network results, ReLU–spline/finite-element connections, compositional regression theory and nonlinear-width bounds. The introduction explicitly credits Lai and Shen's earlier empirical and theoretical dimensionality results. Section 5 additionally connects KANs to additive models, graph networks and kernel methods, beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: There are localized abstract and introduction rewrites, expanded explanatory paragraphs, notation corrections and acknowledgment additions. The six main sections, experimental narrative and Appendices A–F retain their overall organization.

P2.justification: Figure 2.2 is revised to correct edge indices, the original scaling-exponent Table 1 is removed, and the knot-comparison caption is expanded. Several figures and the Appendix A functionality table move relative to surrounding text. The empirical plots and appendix visualizations themselves are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 improves the paper's framing by limiting headline claims, acknowledging comparison-specific weaknesses and giving fuller credit to related theory. The compact-MLP caption provides useful context for parameter-efficiency claims. These are limited gains: empirical validation and uncertainty reporting remain essentially unchanged, and the Feynman width revision is not reconciled with the retained results.
